name: CMS ENERGY CORPORATION

overrides_applied.source: CMS Energy FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-10, accession 0000811156-26-000004), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, line 'Capital expenditures (excludes assets placed under finance lease)': $3,824M for 2025, $3,018M for 2024, $2,407M for 2023. Override value is the filed FY2024 (median-year) figure.
overrides_applied.reason: The engine's capex candidate tags (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment and fallbacks) carry no values after FY2022 in CMS's companyfacts — CMS stopped tagging its cash-flow capital expenditures line under those tags from FY2023. The filing's own cash-flow statement reports the figures above. The override mechanism fills every missing period with one value, so the median year's filed figure ($3,018M) is used for 2023-2025; this is a disclosed approximation — conservative owner's earnings are negative in every one of the three years under the actual per-year figures as well (OCF $2,309M/$2,370M/$2,235M is below capex in each year), so the Tier F conclusion does not depend on the approximation.

overrides_applied.source: CMS Energy FY2025 Form 10-K (filed 2026-02-10, accession 0000811156-26-000004), Note 12 Stock-based Compensation, table 'amounts related to restricted stock awards and restricted stock units': compensation expense recognized for CMS Energy including Consumers was $25M in 2025, $27M in 2024, $28M in 2023. Override value is the filed FY2024 figure.
overrides_applied.reason: CMS files no ShareBasedCompensation or AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense tag in companyfacts at all (the tags are absent, not zero), so the engine gaps SBC for every year. Note 12 of the 10-K reports the actual stock-compensation expense; the single-value override uses the FY2024 figure for all three missing years — the filed range is only $25-28M, so the fill error is at most $3M/yr against a multi-billion-dollar capex gap.

fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
